name: Starting Strength Novice Program
author: Mark Rippetoe (Starting Strength)
summary: A three-day full-body barbell novice program built on the squat, press, bench press, deadlift, power clean and chin-up. You add weight every session for as long as you can, moving through three phases as the deadlift gets too heavy to train three times a week.
evidenceNote: Very low volume per muscle: about 9 work sets of squat a week, 3-6 sets each of press and bench (they alternate, so one gets 2 sessions and the other 1 in a 3-day week), 3 sets of deadlift a week in Phase 1 and fewer later (one set every Day A in Phase 2, every other Day A in Phase 3), and no direct arm, rear-delt or upper-back hypertrophy work until chin-ups arrive in Phase 3 (the FAQ tolerates a few sets of arm work on Friday). It suits true novices who mainly want strength on the barbell lifts. For upper-body muscle growth it is light compared with what hypertrophy research favours, and the late-stage sets of 5 get close to failure as linear progression runs out.

sources.title: Starting Strength Training Programs (Get Started: Programs)
Starting Strength Training Programs (Wayback Machine snapshot 2026-08-12; live page is behind a Cloudflare challenge)

schedule: 3 non-consecutive days per week (e.g. Mon/Wed/Fri), alternating Day A and Day B. Phase 1 (usually 1-3 weeks): A and B differ only by press vs bench. Phase 2 (several weeks to several months): power clean replaces the deadlift on Day B. Phase 3: deadlift and power clean alternate on Day A and chin-ups go on Day B, so the cycle is A(deadlift), B, A(clean), B.

progression.description: Add weight every session. Source (lb): most healthy men 18-35/40 add 10 lb to the squat the first 2-3 times, 15-20 lb to the deadlift the first couple of times then 10 lb for several sessions, after which jumps become 5 lb per workout. Press, bench and power clean may get one 10 lb jump but may need 5 lb from the start, later 2.5 lb or smaller. Converted: squat and deadlift 2.5 kg per session steady-state (early jumps about 5 kg squat for the first 2-3 sessions; deadlift about 7.5-10 kg the first couple of sessions, then about 5 kg for several sessions); press, bench and clean 2.5 kg, then 1.25 kg or smaller. Women and men over 35-40 use smaller jumps. Phase 3 'advanced novice' option: add weight to squats only twice a week and make the middle squat day lighter.
progression.deload: If you miss the prescribed sets and reps, try the same weight next time. If you miss again, deload that lift by 8-10% and work back up with small jumps. After two or three deloads followed by another stall (with sleep and food in order), linear progression on that lift is probably finished.

Once 3x10 at bodyweight is possible, every other chin-up day can be 3x5 weighted, with 3 sets to fatigue at bodyweight on the alternate chin-up days.

notes: The program page lists 'Press/Bench Press' on both days and says they alternate every session. Because Day A and Day B also alternate every session, one pressing lift always lands on the same day; which one depends on what you start with (Press on Day A is shown here). The squat is the low-bar squat as taught in the Starting Strength book. sessionMinutes is an estimate; the program page gives no session length or rest periods.

changes: Confirmed against the official program page and FAQ (read via Wayback snapshots because the live site returns a Cloudflare challenge/403 to automated fetches): all three phases, Day A/B contents, squat 3x5, press/bench 3x5 alternating every session, deadlift 1x5, power clean 5x3 (Phase 2 Day B; alternating with deadlift on Day A in Phase 3), chin-ups on Phase 3 Day B, 3 non-consecutive days/week, phase lengths (Phase 1 usually 1-3 weeks, Phase 2 several weeks to months), lb increments, advanced-novice twice-weekly squat progression, stall rule (repeat once, then deload 8-10%, linear progression done after 2-3 deloads), no-barbell-row substitution and 50+ clean omission, isFree true (free on startingstrength.com). No percentages, AMRAP sets or rest periods are given by the source; restSeconds left null.

Chin-ups: set lastSetAmrap true and rewrote notes: source says bodyweight chins are done for 3 sets to fatigue (every set), and flagged repsLow 1/repsHigh 10 as an app placeholder since the source gives no rep range (10 is only the 3x10 threshold for adding weighted 3x5 days).
Squat warm-up note: clarified the FAQ method (empty bar 2x5, four roughly even jumps from bar to work weight with descending reps 5/3/2), matching the FAQ example.
Progression description: kg conversion now also reflects the source's deadlift step of 10 lb (about 5 kg) for several sessions after the first couple of 15-20 lb jumps.
evidenceNote: '1-3 sets of deadlift' was inaccurate for Phase 3 (deadlift only every other Day A, under one set a week); reworded per phase and noted the FAQ allows a few sets of arm work on Friday.
Added the two Wayback snapshot URLs to sources as readable copies of the official pages.
